description: Starts an AI video generation on the signed-in aicut account, puts the aicut card in front of the user, and returns the new job's id immediately. It does NOT wait for the video. WHEN: the user asks for a video to be made. Call `list_models` first if you have not this session - the `model` id and the allowed values for every other argument come from there, and a combination it does not publish is rejected. AFTER: the video is not ready when this returns, and waiting for it is not something you do by hand. Call `wait_for_generation` with the returned id and `media: "video"`, then follow the two rules below. THE CARD: this call has ALREADY put the aicut card in front of the user, and it fills in the finished media on its own. Do NOT call `show_generation` for this job - that adds a duplicate card; it is only for bringing back an EARLIER generation. HOW TO WAIT: call `wait_for_generation` with this job's id and `media` - it waits server-side and opens no card. While it answers `terminal: false`, wait `poll_after_seconds` and call it again; when `terminal: true`, tell the user in ONE short line what came out. Do not poll `get_video` / `get_image` / `get_audio` instead or spawn timers, and do NOT tell the user the generation is running in between. IF YOU CANNOT RENDER AN AICUT CARD (a terminal or plain SDK client), give the user the `url` from the wait result - aicut cannot see which clients render cards. TIMING: a video usually finishes in 1-3 minutes, and can take up to about 6. Do not assume it failed before then, and do not spawn timers or background shells to wait: call `wait_for_generation` (it waits server-side for up to 15 seconds per call), wait its `poll_after_seconds` and call it again, and stop when it answers `terminal: true`. `get_video` is a single immediate read for one job's raw fields - it is not the waiting loop and must not be polled in one. COST: this spends the user's tokens. Pass `estimate_only: true` first to get the exact price without creating anything - and do that whenever the user has not already agreed to the cost, or when the balance may be tight. SPENDS TOKENS: quote it first (`estimate_only: true`), state the price IN THE SAME MESSAGE as your ask, and wait for a go that names THIS purchase - a bare 'yes' counts only as the direct answer to that priced ask, and an ambiguous one means ask again. The full SPENDING RULES in this server's instructions apply here. IF THE USER REPORTS A CHARGE OR STEP THEY DID NOT EXPECT: re-read your own tool calls and say which you made; aicut cards cannot spend (full rule in this server's instructions). IDEMPOTENCY: `idempotency_key` is optional. Reusing a key REPLAYS the job it first created (even with different settings), so never reuse one to make another generation; the full rules are in this server's instructions (IDEMPOTENCY). OUTPUT: JSON for you to read. Tell the user the media URL plus a one-line summary; do not paste raw JSON, job ids or internal field names.

aspect_ratio.description: Output aspect ratio, one of the model's published `aspect_ratios` (for example `9:16`).

audio.description: Generate audio alongside the video, on the models that support it - `list_models` publishes this parameter for exactly those, and its description there says whether sound costs extra on that model (free on the seedance 2.x family, dearer on kling). IT DEFAULTS TO FALSE: a model sold on native audio still renders SILENT unless you set it, so set it whenever the user asked for sound, dialogue or effects. Never set this to save the user tokens or to make a generation cheaper - set it only when the user explicitly asked for this value, and never carry it over from an earlier request.

character_ids.description: Ids of this account's UPLOADED characters to keep consistent in the video - the `kind: "uploaded"` entries `list_characters` returns, up to 20, in the order they should appear. aicut first draws a start frame that places them, then generates the video from that frame, so the model must accept a start image (every published video model does) and this cannot be combined with `scenes`, `reference_images` or `reference_videos`. COST: the start frame adds a flat 0.2 tokens on top of the video, and `estimate_only: true` includes it. A `cast_member` id belongs to `generate_story_video`, not here.

duration.description: Length in seconds, one of the model's published durations. Longer costs more. Never set this to save the user tokens or to make a generation cheaper - set it only when the user explicitly asked for this value, and never carry it over from an earlier request.

end_image.description: URL of an image the video should end on. Same URL rules as `start_image`.

estimate_only.description: Price these exact settings and create nothing. Returns the token cost, the account balance, and whether the balance covers it. Costs nothing and changes nothing.

idempotency_key.description: Optional retry-safety key. Read the IDEMPOTENCY note in this tool's description before using one - a reused key returns the first job instead of making a new one.

model.description: Model id, exactly as `list_models` returns it (for example `kling-3.0`). Models differ in price by more than any other setting, so use the one the user asked for and never substitute a cheaper model to save them tokens.

prompt.description: What the video should show. The model's `prompt` parameter in `list_models` gives its character limit.

reference_images.description: URLs of images the model should use as style or subject references, on the models that accept them. Same URL rules as `start_image`.

reference_videos.description: URLs of reference videos, on the models that accept them: this account's own uploads and generations, or a genuinely external public video URL (it is downloaded server-side, size-capped, and stored to the account). An aicut-hosted URL that is NOT this account's own media is refused.

resolution.description: Output resolution, one of the model's published options (for example `1080p`). Higher resolutions cost more. Never set this to save the user tokens or to make a generation cheaper - set it only when the user explicitly asked for this value, and never carry it over from an earlier request.

scenes.description: A storyboard: build the video from several scene prompts instead of one, each with its own prompt and duration - the provider cuts its own shots from the whole list and returns ONE video. ONLY ON THE MODELS THAT PUBLISH IT: today that is `kling-3.0` alone, and its bounds are the SAME ones its own webapp picker uses - at most 5 scenes, each 1-15s, totaling 3-15s. Sending this on any other model, or outside those bounds, is refused. Omit `prompt`/`duration`/`start_image`/`end_image`/`reference_images` when using this - each scene carries its own prompt and duration, and this call still needs `model` plus whatever ELSE the model requires (e.g. `resolution`, `aspect_ratio` - both stay REQUIRED, they are not per-scene). Price this with `estimate_only: true` first: it is priced as one generation of the scenes' combined duration, not per scene.

duration.description: This scene's own length in seconds.

prompt.description: What THIS scene shows. Each scene is its own beat, not a continuation.

start_image.description: URL of an image to start the video from. Either a public https URL (aicut fetches and stores it) or a URL an earlier generation on this same account returned.

name: generate_video
title: Generate an AI video
